answer: The coastguard fires rockets in drill every month and the station keeper logs each firing, the wind and the range, and only a station with a clean log may answer a wreck. A island rocket fired without a log fails the station: the pearl of the shore must show the drill the keeper recorded, and an unlogged rocket leaves the crew unready. Faking the drills means keeping a station for a year, firing 60 rockets and paying 9,600, while the tide entry in the station book is read by the inspector each spring, so a crew whose drills were never logged is struck off the roll.
